All corrections verified against the bytes. My spot-checks confirm every load-bearing claim from the verification votes. Here is the synthesis.

---

# Muse 6.0 (macOS / v9 wave) — Synthesis

Scope: Mac only. Static analysis of the Meta-signed/notarized 6.0 DMG against the prior 4.1 build. Base paths (all absolute): app `extracted/v9/Muse.app`, prior app `extracted/release-audit-2026-09-27/Muse.app`, prepared material `extracted/v9/prep/` (referenced below as `prep/<file>:<line>`). Scratch: `extracted/v9/work/mac-synth/`.

Survivorship: of the 9 findings put to the two adversarial lenses, **none were refuted** — 4 are `confirmed` by both, 5 are `partially_confirmed` by both (core holds, specifics corrected). All 9 SURVIVE. Two further findings (extension removal, approval fail-closed) were not formally voted but are corroborated by all three finders and I re-verified them directly.

---

## 1. Verdict

**Consent-gated surveillance-grade collection with named weaknesses.** Muse 6.0 is a Meta-backend-driven agent with a full-desktop computer-use surface (Accessibility + synthetic input + ScreenCaptureKit), shell execution, native browser control, location, and six OS-data connectors — surveillance-grade *capability* — but every data source is fronted by a macOS TCC grant and/or a consent sheet, approval fails closed, and no covert channel was found. 6.0 **reduces** covert surface versus 4.1 (the bundled Chrome extension and the `stealth.min.js` anti-detection kit are deleted). The label rests on breadth of consented collection plus named weaknesses, not on hidden exfiltration.

---

## 2. What changed from 4.1 (the heart)

**Removed (attack/covert surface reduced):**
- The entire bundled Manifest-V3 Chrome extension `Resources/chrome/` (verified absent in 6.0; present in 4.1 with `background.js`, `hatch-web-pairing.js`, `lib/`, `manifest.json`, …) and `Resources/stealth.min.js` (180,440 bytes, 4.1 only). The puppeteer-extra stealth/anti-bot-detection kit leaves the product.
- Native CDP/extension bridge: `cdpError`, `cdpNotReady`, `webSocketDebuggerUrl`, `.hatch-extension-stamp`, `Library/Application Support/Hatch/ChromeExtension` all dropped (`prep/strings-removed-in-6.0.txt:1321-1322,1680,175,765`).
- The only removed host is `http://127.0.0.1:` — the CDP loopback endpoint (4.1 `prep/muse41.strings.txt:7406`), **not** an "extension WebSocket gateway" (the 4.1 extension references no loopback). A bare `127.0.0.1` persists in 6.0 inside the QUIC library.
- Synthetic-mouse primitives `_CGEventCreateMouseEvent` / `_CGEventPostToPid` (`prep/imports-diff-4.1-6.0.txt:243-244`), replaced by SkyLight `SLEventPostToPid=` (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:30`).

**Added / expanded:**
- **ScreenCaptureKit** screen-capture backend: `SCStream` / `_SCStreamFrameInfoStatus` imports new (`prep/imports-diff-4.1-6.0.txt:288-289`; `prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:3183`), replacing 4.1's AVCapture path.
- Finer computer-control primitives: `hold_key, release_key, left_mouse_down, left_mouse_up, left_press, set_window_frame` (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:35`).
- **One new entitlement**, the only entitlement change: `com.apple.security.personal-information.location => true` (`prep/entitlements-diff-4.1-6.0.txt:13`).
- **New per-app auto-sync switch UI** (native): switch labels + settings-page copy for Contacts/Calendar/Reminders/Notes, e.g. "*New and changed contacts are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for*" (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:3345-3346,2846-2850`) — **absent from 4.1 native**.
- **New diagnostics channels**: `reliability_event_log_upload` endpoint (6.0=1, 4.1=0), Apple **MetricKit** subscription (`MXMetricManagerSubscriber`/`didReceiveDiagnosticPayloads:`, 6.0=2, 4.1=0), and `HatchAppleDiagnostics`/`apple_diagnostic_ping_id` (6.0=4, 4.1=0).
- **New agent-permission disclosure rows**: "*the assistant driving a web browser on the user's behalf*" and "*…running shell/terminal commands on the user's computer*" (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:1082-1083`).
- **Confidential-VM machinery** (privacy-positive): recovery-PIN enrollment (`index60.main.pretty.js:321124`) and telemetry suppression on confidential/unconfirmed VM routes (`index60.main.pretty.js:12244,317051`).
- `Info.plist`: `AnalyticsUserAgentAppName=EndoForMacOS`, `FBBuildNumber=1082791187`, version 4.1→6.0 (`prep/infoplist-diff-4.1-6.0.txt`).
- `metaconfig.json`: dropped alpha/TestFlight/Canada-rollout/`falco_qpl_transport` keys; added `hatch_voice_design_enabled` (default-off), `hatch_us_pjs` — a GA transition (`prep/metaconfig-diff-4.1-6.0.txt`).
- Sizes: native binary 19,513,888 → 22,262,272 bytes; web bundle 53,200,854 → 44,500,720 bytes (verified).

**Unchanged:** Sparkle 2.7.0-beta.1/2040, feed `facebook.com/endo/release/appcast.xml?channel=production`, pinned `SUPublicEDKey` (verified); LocalConnectorHITL fail-closed; server proactive-sync flag; `ios_breakpad_crash_logs` crash URL; `analytics_events` identity schema; no LaunchAgent/Daemon/XPC; all four helper binaries byte-identical to 4.1 outside UUID+signature.

**Net new endpoints:** none off-Meta. Added native hosts are `www.instagram.com`, `www.meta.com` (marketing links) plus two inert Meta networking-library host constants new in 6.0 — `ohttp-gateway.atmeta.com` (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:5631`) and `igcdn-origincache-internal-services-all.fbcdn.net` (`:5213`).

---

## 3. Surviving findings (tagged, with locators, proof level)

**F1 — Full-desktop computer-use agent; expanded in 6.0, multi-gated.** `[REMOTE_CONTROL · GATED · WEAKNESS]` — proof: **reachable**. `confirmed`×2.
Observe (AXUIElement), control (click/type/key/drag/scroll/menu + new `hold_key`/`left_mouse_down`/`up`/`left_press`/`set_window_frame`), screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit, across any app. Gate: TCC Accessibility + Screen Recording (`prep/muse60.strings.txt:9734`); server flags `hatch_desktop:enable_computer_control`/`enable_browser_automation`/`endo_enable_screen_recording` (`:7036-7042`); per-action approval; preview+Stop ("*Starting a session does not grant control permission. If user_can_see_preview is false, tell the user*" `:9557`); send/pay/delete forced last. **Weaknesses (verifier-added):** "Always allow" grants never expire (`index60.main.pretty.js:305724`); the preview is a *soft* gate — input is posted in the background and "*never brings apps to the front*", so visibility reduces to the model honoring the tell-the-user instruction; server flags can flip availability remotely; `VALID_HITL_MODES` includes `disabled` (`index60.main.pretty.js:47523,48145`, scoped to connector egress).

**F2 — Browser control is native "agent window"; the extension/CDP path was retired, not replaced.** `[REMOTE_CONTROL · GATED]` — proof: **reachable**. `confirmed`×2.
4.1 already instructed the agent "*The browser and browser.proxy device commands are no longer supported. Use computer.control and screen.snap…*" (`prep/muse41.strings.txt:7409`) and carried the full native surface; 6.0 deleted the vestigial CDP/extension files. Browsers enumerated natively (Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Firefox/Arc/Kagi/Vivaldi/Opera/Zen, `prep/muse60.strings.txt:9900-9932`). **Corrects the task's own premise** that something "replaced" the extension in 6.0 — nothing did.

**F3 — Bundled Chrome extension + `stealth.min.js` removed.** `[WEAKNESS]` — proof: **present**. Cross-corroborated (not formally voted); directly re-verified. The anti-detection capability left the product; it was already unreferenced by the 4.1 native binary.

**F4 — Shell / `system.run` execution, per-program-gated; unchanged.** `[REMOTE_CONTROL · GATED]` — proof: **reachable**. `confirmed`×2.
`permission.system.run.read/.write/.which`, broad `alwaysAllow` cleared → per-program grants (`prep/muse60.strings.txt:7221-7226`); `NSTask`/`posix_spawn` imported (`prep/muse60.undef.txt`). Consent row is **new 6.0 copy** (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:1083`). No server flag enables it (negative result over `metaconfig.json`); filesystem+shell blocked from local-connector stores.

**F5 — Proactive-sync default is server-governed and default-ON; the prior "no in-app toggle" claim is now FALSE.** `[CONSENT_BYPASS · GATED · WEAKNESS]` — proof: **reachable** (default-ON fallback). `partially_confirmed`×2 (SURVIVES, corrected).
Server flag `endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled` still resolves the default (`prep/muse60.strings.txt:7244`, `featured_app_setting_changed:7250`); client fallback is `useState(autoSync.enabled ?? true)` (`index60.main.pretty.js:272290`). **Correction:** 6.0 adds visible per-connector/per-app auto-sync switches with disclosure copy for Contacts/Calendar/Reminders/Notes ("*shared automatically. Turn this off*", `prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:2846-2850,3345-3346`); a web `LocalConnectorAutoSyncRow` toggle existed in both builds. The control gap the prior report flagged is **closed**; the residual concern is the *pre-checked, server-settable default*, not absence of a control.

**F6 — Approval baseline fails closed to requires-approval.** `[GATED]` — proof: **reachable**. Corroborated across all three finders (the fail-closed string also appears in F4/F5 votes).
"*[LocalConnectorHITL] Permission default unavailable; inherited access requires approval*" (`prep/muse60.strings.txt:11025`). Protective property. (The prior report's cited address `Muse 0xc46220` is not re-verifiable without disassembly; the behavior strings are intact.)

**F7 — Location: only the entitlement is new; code + usage strings pre-existed; WhenInUse-only; geofencing NOT wired.** `[GATED · UNDISCLOSED]` — proof: **reachable**. `partially_confirmed`×2 (SURVIVES, substantially corrected).
Only entitlement delta is `location=true` (`prep/entitlements-diff-4.1-6.0.txt:13`). **Corrections:** `NSLocation*UsageDescription` are byte-identical in 4.1/6.0 (absent from `prep/infoplist-diff`) and CoreLocation symbols are unchanged (no entry in `prep/symbols-diff-4.1-6.0.txt`) — so "ACTIVATED in 6.0" is overstated; one lens argues the entitlement is largely **cosmetic** for this non-sandboxed hardened-runtime app (location was already TCC-reachable in 4.1). The `significantLocation`/`geofence` tokens are `NodeSyncSerializer` trigger-enum labels, **not** CoreLocation monitoring calls — `startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges`, `startMonitoringForRegion`, `requestAlwaysAuthorization` are **absent in both builds** (negative result). Demonstrable mechanism is foreground `startUpdatingLocation` under WhenInUse, feeding the in-app MapLibre map; **not** exposed as a VM agent tool. Gate: macOS WhenInUse TCC prompt + disclosed usage string.

**F8 — Crash + telemetry carry identities; diagnostics EXPANDED in 6.0.** `[UNDISCLOSED · CONSENT_BYPASS]` — proof: **present/reachable**; client telemetry **default_on**. `partially_confirmed`×2 (SURVIVES, corrected).
Crashpad → `facebook.com/mobile/ios_breakpad_crash_logs/` (both builds, `prep/muse60.strings.txt:12572`); `analytics_events` stores `app_identity`/`device_identity`/`user_identity`/`event_payload` (`:17358`); `telemetryAllowed` gate (`:11673`) and crash-disable toggle (`:16627`) exist. Client telemetry defaults on: `getItem(CLIENT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED_KEY) !== 'false'` (`index60.main.pretty.js:12213`); AI-training preference defaults on: `trainingEnabled ?? true` ("*Allow us to use your interactions with {product} to develop and improve AI at Meta*", `:309419`). **Corrections:** `reliability_event_log_upload` is **NEW in 6.0** (6.0=1, 4.1=0) — not "both in 4.1"; MetricKit + `HatchAppleDiagnostics` are new; so the channel is **strengthened**, not unchanged. One lens would reduce tags to `[GATED]` because default-on is not statically provable for the crash/native path; the web client-telemetry default-on *is* provable. New **CVM telemetry suppression** is privacy-positive (`:12244,317051`).

**F9 — Auto-update via Sparkle 2.7.0-beta.1/2040 (pre-CVE), EdDSA-pinned facebook.com feed.** `[PERSISTENCE · WEAKNESS · GATED]` — proof: **reachable**. `confirmed`×2.
Version 2.7.0-beta.1/2040 (verified); `SUFeedURL=…facebook.com/endo/release/appcast.xml?channel=production`, `SUPublicEDKey=disxTjHFQiufTKeFl5u0U+72690NzNIoqakG/XAEasw=` (verified); `endo_rollout:minimum_supported_app_version` server force-upgrade (`prep/muse60.strings.txt:9248`). **Corrections:** "forced on" is not statically provable (no `SUEnableAutomaticChecks` in Info.plist; a `updaterShouldPromptForPermissionToCheckForUpdates:` delegate exists, `:31941`); "pre-CVE-2025-10016" is an external version-to-CVE attribution (the *version* is proven; CVE applicability is not provable from the sample). Gate: appcast EdDSA-signed, key pinned (per established facts the 6.0 DMG verifies and a one-bit flip is rejected). Residual weakness = the un-upgraded pre-hardening Sparkle beta.

**F10 — Endpoint stability: all collection to documented Meta hosts; no new non-Meta destination.** `[UNDISCLOSED]` — proof: **present**. `partially_confirmed`×2 (SURVIVES, corrected).
All data endpoints (`agent.meta.ai`, `api.meta.ai`, `hatch-api.meta.ai`, `auth.meta.com`, `scontent.xx.fbcdn.net`, `www.facebook.com`, `wss://shortwave.facebook.com`) unchanged. **Corrections:** the enumeration missed two Meta networking-lib host constants new in 6.0 (`ohttp-gateway.atmeta.com`, `igcdn-origincache-internal-services-all.fbcdn.net`) and the web-bundle embed/social/CDN hosts; the removed host is the CDP loopback, not an extension gateway. Substantive conclusion (no new off-Meta exfil) holds.

**F11 — Config/label delta benign; orphaned extension residuals.** `[UNDISCLOSED]` — proof: **present**. `confirmed`×2.
metaconfig GA cleanup; `AnalyticsUserAgentAppName=EndoForMacOS`/`FBBuildNumber` added. The Chrome bundle-id `com.google.chrome.app.mdpkiol…` sits in a **blocked-apps** list (`setBlockedAppsSettings`), and `/tmp/endo-native-messaging.sock` persists — both present in 4.1, now **orphaned** (no bundled extension to drive them).

---

## 4. Strongest evidence for / against the spyware label

**FOR (why "surveillance-grade"):**
- Remote-driven full-desktop control + shell + browser + 6 OS connectors, all actionable by Meta's model backend (F1, F2, F4).
- Every connector sync still defaults ON (server flag + `?? true`), and client telemetry and AI-training-on-your-interactions both default ON (F5, F8).
- Diagnostics broadened in 6.0 (reliability endpoint + MetricKit + Apple diagnostics), events keyed to `user_identity`/`session_id`, with no ordinary-user crash/diagnostics opt-out located (F8).
- Soft spots in the consent model: never-expiring "Always allow", a background-input preview that never foregrounds, server-flippable capability flags, a `disabled` HITL mode (F1).

**AGAINST (why not covert spyware):**
- **No covert channel found** (negative result, all three finders): every documented source — Notes/Mail/Calendar/Reminders/Contacts/Messages/WhatsApp/Files/computer-control/location — is fronted by a consent sheet and/or TCC grant, and approval fails closed (F6).
- 6.0 **removed** the anti-detection `stealth.min.js` and the standalone CDP channel (F3) — a *reduction* in covert surface.
- No new off-Meta endpoint; all flows to previously-documented Meta infrastructure; added hosts are marketing links + inert Meta networking constants (F10).
- No persistence beyond a visible `SMAppService` "Run on startup" toggle — no LaunchAgent/Daemon/XPC; all four helper binaries byte-identical to 4.1 outside signature; Crashpad uses Mach bootstrap, not an on-disk plist (negative results, Report 3 MAC6-04).
- Per-file inventory: every 6.0 file matches the Meta seal, no trailing/steganographic bytes.
- The previously-flagged "no in-app sync toggle" gap is now closed (F5).

---

## 5. Prior-report corrections (claims now wrong or imprecise)

1. **Task/README premise "explain what replaced the extension for browser control" is misleading** — nothing replaced it in 6.0; the native `computer.control`/agent-window path was already active in 4.1 (`prep/muse41.strings.txt:7409`). 6.0 only deleted the deprecated CDP/extension files.
2. **"NSLocation(WhenInUse)UsageDescription strings were added in 6.0" is WRONG** — byte-identical in 4.1 and 6.0 (not in `prep/infoplist-diff`); CoreLocation code pre-existed. Only the entitlement bit is new, and its runtime effect is disputed (likely cosmetic for a non-sandboxed app).
3. **"Calendar/Reminders/Contacts have no in-app auto-sync switch" is now FALSE for 6.0** — native per-app switches + a settings page were added (`prep/strings-new-in-6.0.txt:3345-3346,2846-2850`); a web auto-sync row existed in both builds.
4. **README §6/§7 (Chrome-extension broad debugger access; `stealth.min.js` bot-evasion) no longer describe 6.0** — both deleted.
5. **"Significant-change monitoring / geofencing" on Mac is not substantiated** — those tokens are sync-trigger enum labels; the CoreLocation monitoring selectors are absent in both builds; only WhenInUse foreground updates are wired.
6. **`reliability_event_log_upload` is NEW in 6.0**, not a 4.1 carry-over; the crash/diagnostics surface is expanded, not "unchanged."
7. **Crash handler is Google Crashpad**, not Breakpad — only the URL token `ios_breakpad_crash_logs` retains the legacy name.
8. **"Auto-update forced on" is not statically provable** — no `SUEnableAutomaticChecks` key; a permission-prompt delegate exists. Characterize as wired/reachable.
9. **The removed `127.0.0.1` was the CDP loopback endpoint, not an "extension WebSocket gateway."**
10. **Shell/`system.run`** was present in 4.1 but omitted from the prior Mac tool table — add it. **CROSS-PLATFORM.md** Mac location row should move from "not established" to "entitlement present, TCC WhenInUse-gated, map-only, not a VM tool."

---

## 6. What static analysis cannot settle

- **Live default booleans**: the server values of `featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled`, `enable_computer_control`/`enable_browser_automation`/`endo_enable_screen_recording`, `minimum_supported_app_version`, and the native crash/`telemetryAllowed` enable state. The *gates and client-side defaults* are visible; the server's current booleans are not.
- **Whether the location entitlement has any runtime effect** on this non-sandboxed binary (the two lenses disagree); and whether location is ever transmitted (it is wired to the map UI and a sync-trigger enum, not observed on the wire).
- **Actual transmission** of telemetry/crash/diagnostics payloads and their exact field contents — present and reachable in code; not demonstrable without execution/network capture (excluded by the rules).
- **Whether the client-telemetry settings toggle is employee-gated** — a user-facing label "*Send browser analytics, performance measurements, and error reports*" renders (`index60.main.pretty.js:317051`), but whether the section is restricted to employees was not resolved statically.
- **Runtime enforcement of the HITL/approval model** — the fail-closed strings and per-action approval UI are present; whether a fresh install ever runs a read with no prompt, and how `EndoNodeAllowAllHITLGating` and the `disabled` HITL mode are actually invoked, require dynamic analysis.
- **The pre-CVE Sparkle exposure** — version is proven; exploitability/CVE applicability was not reproduced (and the pinned-signature feed mitigates the MITM path).

ONE REFINEMENT to the finding's wording: calling the 4.1 extension purely 'vestigial' is slightly too strong. 4.1 still actively recommended a live CDP 'browser' tool (string 'Use the browser tool instead ... browser controls external Chrome through live CSS selectors', removed in 6.0), so 4.1 ran two parallel browser-control paths and 6.0 is a CONSOLIDATION onto the pre-existing native path, not merely deletion of dead files. The strongest gate, macOS TCC (verified via AXIsProcessTrusted imports for Accessibility and ScreenCaptureKit linkage for Screen Recording), is OS-enforced and cannot be bypassed by Meta's server flags — this defeats any "covert" reading, so I cannot refute the finding. # Muse Android v9 (9.0.0.23.178) — Synthesis

## 1. One-line verdict

**Consent-gated surveillance-grade collection with named weaknesses** — and v9 is a *net reduction* in collection surface versus the prior build (the entire agent photo subsystem, on-device ML Kit image labelling, and four media permissions were removed), with no covert channel found at the container, native, or network-surface level.

## 2. WHAT CHANGED vs 9.0.0.11.178 (the heart)

All three finders agree on the version and the subtractive nature of the delta; I byte-verified the load-bearing items.

**Identity / integrity**
- versionCode `1061401140 → 1061401224`; versionName `9.0.0.11.178 → 9.0.0.23.178` (`and-new-manifest.txt:3`). Both Meta-signed (provenance pre-established).
- 36/36 native `.so` **byte-identical** to 9.0.0.11; DEX host set **byte-identical** (71 hosts, 0 added / 0 removed); Falco/analytics2/graphservice telemetry strings byte-identical (report 3, `work/container-net/dexhosts-v9.txt`). The "3 new realtime hosts" (`genai-hatch-realtime`, `genai-kepler-realtime`, `meta-ai-realtime`.facebook.com) were a **jadx-decompilation false alarm** — present in both v11 and v9 DEX.

**Capabilities REMOVED (privacy-positive)**
- **Four permissions dropped, zero added (65 → 61):** `ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION`, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`(maxSdk32), `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED` (`and-manifest-names-diff.txt`). I confirmed CAMERA, location, SMS, contacts, calendar, call-log, 19 health categories, boot and notification-listener bindings are all **retained**.
- **Entire `com/facebook/aura/commands/photos/` package deleted** (54 files incl. PhotosUploadHandler, PhotoUploadWorker, DeviceMediaStoreReader, PhotoLabelScanner, MediaDeviceSyncClient). Verified: `ls commands/photos/` → *No such file or directory*; `grep -i photo X/AbstractC17146nu.java` → 0 hits (no photo handler imported into the registry).
- **Command handlers 42 → 39:** PHOTOS_SEARCH / PHOTOS_UPLOAD / PHOTOS_UPLOAD_STATUS unregistered. `HatchNodeCommandRegistry.Companion.isCommandRegistered` scans 39 indices (`HatchNodeCommandRegistry.java:55` `if (i >= 39) return false`), and PHOTOS_SEARCH is not among them.
- **ML Kit / on-device image labelling removed:** manifest `MlKitComponentDiscoveryService` + Common/Vision/ThinLabel registrars gone; 7 MLKit `.properties` version-pins removed; DEX `'mlkit'` 39 → 0 (report 3). No MLKit `.so`/`.tflite` remain.

**Unchanged structure**
- Data sources unchanged at 12 (alarms, battery, calendar, call_log, contacts, geofences, health, location, network_state, notifications, reminders, sms). No new commands, gates, endpoints, permissions, or exported components. Only one manifest component removed (`MlKitComponentDiscoveryService`); everything else byte/structurally identical.

**New surface (benign)**

## 3. Surviving findings (with locators, tagged)

**F1 — Agent photo collection removed end-to-end** — tags: **GATED** (structurally OFF) · proof: reachable · SURVIVED (consensus; report 3's contrary finding corrected, see §5).
`registry.findByWireId("photos.*")` → null → UNKNOWN_COMMAND ("The requested command is not available on this device." `HatchNodeClient.java:1877-1889`). Not advertised: capabilities derive from `getEnabledCommandSpecs()` over the 39 registered handlers (`HatchCapabilitiesSnapshot.java:178`, `NodeRegistrationInfo` registration ~`:2319`). Connector predicate `LocalDeviceConnectorKt$…$3.invoke()` returns `isNodesMediaEnabled()` only `if (isCommandRegistered(PHOTOS_SEARCH))` — **hard-false** (verified). Re-enabling needs an app update, not a server flag.

**F2 — Four media permissions removed; PhotoAccessUtils now dead code** — tags: **GATED, WEAKNESS** · proof: default_on · SURVIVED.
`PhotoAccessUtils` still calls `checkSelfPermission` on the four now-undeclared permissions, so `isReadGranted()` is permanently false and the `@photos` pseudo-permission is never added (`HatchNodeCommandRegistry.currentGrantedSet()`). EXIF-GPS gallery reads (via `ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION`) are now unreachable.

**F3 — `is_nodes_media_enabled` MobileConfig flag inert** — tags: **GATED** · proof: reachable · SURVIVED.
`MC.java` `hatch_media_sync` CONFIG_ID 139538, `is_nodes_media_enabled = …A0p(36312977825071430L)` persists, but gated behind the hard-false `isCommandRegistered(PHOTOS_SEARCH)` client check. Server flip cannot re-enable photos.

**F4 — Backfill has no connection-date clamp / no minimum floor; contacts = full address book** — tags: **GATED, WEAKNESS** · proof: reachable · SURVIVED *in corrected form* (the imprecise "null start_date → full history" claim was DROPPED — refuted + partially-refuted; the precise claim was confirmed + confirmed).
`HatchNodeClient.handleReservedDataSourceCommand` reads `start_date`/`end_date` as optional, requires only `source` ("source is required"), and passes the server-supplied value straight to `DataSource.backfill` with **no floor tied to connect time** (`DataSourcePublishPipeline.deliver` windows down only to the server `start`). The four time-series sources **require a non-null `start_date`** but accept an arbitrarily early one (verified: `SmsDataSource.java:204`, `CallLogDataSource.java:193`, `CalendarDataSource.java:211`, `HealthDataSource.java:638-639` all `"start_date is required…"`). Contacts accepts null→"" and sweeps the **whole address book** via `deliverPaged` (`ContactsDataSource.java:237,244`; `DeviceContactsReader.readContactPage` selects `_id > ?`, no date). `isUserEnabled` defaults true (`HatchDataSourceRegistry.java:37`).

**F5 — `location.get` and `geofence.*` carry no HITL (OS location permission only)** — tags: **CONSENT_BYPASS, WEAKNESS** · severity **high** · proof: reachable · SURVIVED (confirmed + confirmed).
`NodeHitlCatalog.forCommand` returns null for LOCATION_GET and GEOFENCE_SET/REMOVE/LIST (and NETWORK_STATE/BATTERY_GET); `forDataSource` maps only health/contacts/calendar/call_log/sms/notifications (default null). `HatchNodeClient` enters `hitlGate.check(...)` only when the spec is non-null, so these execute with **no per-action approval card**, unlike every other sensitive source. Handlers are registered/reachable (`X/AbstractC17146nu.java` LocationGetHandler + 3 Geofence handlers). The `NodeHitlGroup.LOCATION` enum exists but is never wired. Gate = OS `ACCESS_FINE/COARSE/BACKGROUND_LOCATION` only.

**F6 — `network_state` + `battery` publish on every app-open, no HITL** — tags: **CONSENT_BYPASS, WEAKNESS** (report-2 verifiers also upheld **COVERT_COLLECTION** on mechanism) · proof: default_on · SURVIVED (3 confirming votes).
Both declare `proactiveTrigger=AppOpen`, `proactiveDelivery=TRANSIENT`, `isEnabled()=true` (`NetworkStateDataSource.java:34-35`, `BatteryDataSource.java:39-40`). In `ProactiveSyncRunner.run` (baksmali, `work/android-reverify/…/ProactiveSyncRunner.smali`) a null HITL spec `if-eqz` jumps past `NodeHitlGate.check`. Battery has an **empty** permission list; network_state needs only auto-granted `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`. `HatchProactiveSyncCatchUpJob` fires AppOpen sources in foreground. *Read:* mechanically covert (no prompt, no in-app disclosure) but **low-sensitivity payload** (connectivity type, battery level); durable retention/transmission not shown. I carry it as CONSENT_BYPASS + WEAKNESS, COVERT_COLLECTION noted as mechanism-only.

**F7 — `PermissionDefaultMode.fromWire(null/unknown) → AUTO_ALLOW` reaches enforcement once settings are cached; fail-closed only pre-cache** — tags: **CONSENT_BYPASS, WEAKNESS** · proof: reachable (production baseline server-held) · SURVIVED (report-1 instance CONTESTED by one lens; report-2 instance confirmed + confirmed; **I byte-settled it in favor of CONSENT_BYPASS**).
`PermissionDefaultMode.java:42` `return …== null ? AUTO_ALLOW : …`. Decisive: `PermissionDefaultsStore.write()` **unconditionally** persists `connectorDefault.getWireValue()` (`:29`), and `read()` uses `fromWire` (`:45`); so a server response that *omits* `connector_default` is cached as `"auto_allow"`, `hasCachedSettings()` (`:64`, key-presence) becomes true, and `cachedConnectorDefault()` returns AUTO_ALLOW to the gate (`PermissionSettingsRepository.java:309-315`). Under AUTO_ALLOW an unset READ resolves ALLOW (`NodeHitlPermissionStore.getMode` → `withBaseline(defaultFor(READ)=ALLOW)` = ALLOW) → **no prompt**. `HatchNotificationFilterManager` installs only `WorkAppNotificationFilter` (inert on consumer devices) + `BlockedAppsNotificationFilter`; default `PhoneNotificationsAccessMode = ALL` blocks nothing (`HatchGatewayPrefsStore.getPhoneNotificationsAccessMode` → ALL when unset). ## 4. Strongest evidence FOR vs AGAINST the spyware label

**FOR "spyware" (weaknesses that make consent softer than the UI implies):**
- Server-held HITL baseline where a *missing* `connector_default` normalizes to **auto_allow** and reaches enforcement (F7) — unset reads of SMS/call_log/contacts/calendar/notifications can publish with no prompt, a server-side decision.
- Location + geofence actions get **no per-action consent card** at all (F5), gated only by a one-time OS permission — weaker than the sibling sensitive sources that do prompt.
- Backfill has **no connection-date floor** (F4); a server can request history predating "connect," and contacts is pulled in full.
- Breadth: SMS, call-log, contacts, calendar, 19 health categories, all notifications, location, geofences — a genuinely surveillance-grade sensor set, re-armed across reboot/update (F9).

**AGAINST "spyware":**
- **No covert channel** (report 3): APK bytes fully accounted (no prepend/append, 4 standard signing-block IDs only), code-transparency 41/41 executables attested-match, 36/36 `.so` byte-identical, DEX host set byte-identical, all device-data publish routes through the single first-party Hatch gateway to cert-pinned Meta hosts.
- Every powerful capability sits behind a **real gate**: OS runtime permissions, a heavy OS Notification-Access grant, a server+HITL layer that *fails closed pre-cache*, FOA UID checks, and a radio provider **hardcoded off** (F11).
- v9 **shrinks** the surface: agent photo read/upload removed end-to-end (F1-F3), on-device image labelling removed, four media permissions dropped — the opposite of a tightening surveillance build.
- Nothing is collected that bypasses the gateway; no new identifier or content egress path vs 9.0.0.11.

## 5. Prior-report corrections

1. **`RELEASE-AUDIT-2026-09-27.md §3`** — "All 65 declared uses-permission entries are unchanged" is **now wrong** for 9.0.0.23: 61 permissions; the four media/photo perms were removed. (19 health categories remain.)
2. **Prior spyware finding #5** ("photos.upload behind `is_nodes_media_enabled`, default off") must be downgraded to **REMOVED** for 9.0.0.23: handlers are deleted (photos.* → UNKNOWN_COMMAND), not advertised, no declared media permission, connector predicate hard-false. The flag is present but non-actuating.
3. **On-device ML Kit image labelling** is no longer a present capability (registrars/service, `MlKitPhotoLabeler`, `PhotoLabelScanner` removed). `ANDROID.md §6` (Photos) is stale; `ANDROID.md:48` (ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION) and `:87`/`:218` (photos in the auto_allow no-prompt set) must drop photos.
4. **The "backfill with no lower date bound" shorthand is a misread** (and predates v9 — the guards exist verbatim in 9.0.0.11): SMS/call_log/calendar/health **require** a non-null `start_date` (reject null with `missing_start_date`); **notifications is not backfillable** (`supportsBackfill=false`); only contacts accepts null. The accurate, still-true claim is "no clamp to connection time / no minimum floor, and contacts = full address book."
5. **This pass's report 3 (`V9-PHOTO-UPLOAD-PERSISTS`) overstates persistence** and conflicts with the dispatch-path evidence: `PHOTOS_UPLOAD` (enum id 22) and `is_nodes_media_enabled` survive, but as **vestigial** symbols — the agent cannot invoke photo upload (no handler → UNKNOWN_COMMAND, not advertised, predicate hard-false). The `rupload`/`MediaUpload`/`PhotoPicker` machinery it cites is **general/user-driven** upload infra (composer, SMS/MMS attachment, voice-avatar assets — `rupload` in the aura tree appears only in `HatchAvatarAssetServiceKt`), not an agent gallery-upload capability. Treat photo collection as **removed**, with user-initiated Photo-Picker upload (permissionless, user-selected only) as the sole remaining path.
6. **Radio provider** — report 1's "server-gated, default not determinable" is superseded by report 2's (verified) `getRadioSignalProviderEnabled(){return false;}` — client-side hardcoded off.
7. **`fromWire` mitigation** — report 1 AND-V9-07's framing ("native proactive-sync HITL path fails closed") is only half-true: fail-closed is **pre-cache only**; once any settings response is cached, an omitted/unknown `connector_default` is persisted as `auto_allow` and becomes the enforcement baseline. CONSENT_BYPASS stands.
8. Minor: notification-listener manifest locator is `and-new-manifest.txt:542-543` (one finder cited 564-565; excerpt text correct).

## 6. What static analysis cannot settle

- **Production server values:** the connector/network HITL baseline actually sent (`auto_allow` vs `always_ask`), and whether the server ever omits `connector_default` — the single input that decides whether F7 silently auto-allows reads in the field. Also the AD_ID egress server setting. (The radio-provider default **is** settled: client hardcodes false.)
- **Actual transmission/retention:** that `network_state`/`battery` TRANSIENT snapshots (F6) are durably retained Meta-side, and more generally that *any* payload leaves the device — no live traffic was observed (static-only, per rules; no Meta/Facebook/meta.ai/hatch host contacted).
- **Server-fetched approval/disclosure copy:** the per-category HITL prompt text and consent wording are fetched at runtime, so the disclosure itself is not statically auditable.
- **FOA UID/signature allowlist internals** (F10): the peer allowlist lives in the obfuscated `com.meta.foa` native/lib layer, not reconstructed.
- Scope note: android only — iOS HatchApp and macOS were not reasoned about here.

*Method/compliance: static analysis only; nothing under `…/musefuck` modified; no binary/JS executed, no extension loaded, no Meta host contacted. Spot-checks were read-only `grep`/`cat`/`sed` over the prepared jadx tree; no scratch files were needed.*

votes.corrected_claim: The reserved data_source.backfill handler in HatchNodeClient.handleReservedDataSourceCommand (9.0.0.23.178) reads start_date/end_date as optional JSON params (null when absent) and requires only the source id ("source is required"), passing null through to DataSource.backfill(startDate, endDate, ...). That component-level behavior is CONFIRMED and unchanged. HOWEVER the finding's stated consequence -- a null start_date "giving no lower bound (full history)" for the sensitive sources -- is REFUTED. Each time-series sensitive connector re-validates and REJECTS a null/empty start_date before reading: SmsDataSource returns missing_start_date "start_date is required for sms backfill"; CallLogDataSource "start_date is required for call_log backfill"; CalendarDataSource "start_date is required for calendar backfill"; HealthDataSource "start_date is required for health backfill". So for sms/call_log/calendar/health there IS a connector-level lower-bound requirement; null yields an error, not full history. Also, notifications is NOT a backfillable source: NotificationsDataSource.supportsBackfill = false, so backfill falls through to the default impl returning backfill_not_supported. Of the six listed sources only contacts actually accepts null (ContactsDataSource coerces null startDate to "" and proceeds) -- but contacts carry no date dimension, so "no lower date bound" is vacuous there, and the contacts read is still behind the auto-sync switch, read-access Allow, READ_CONTACTS permission, and a forDataSource CONTACTS/READ HITL. Confirmed gate facts: HatchDataSourceRegistry.isUserEnabled defaults to true; NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource returns a READ spec for exactly health, contacts, calendar, call_log, sms, notifications and null otherwise. # Muse iOS v9 (HatchApp 9.1.0, build 1080826056) — Spyware Synthesis

## 1. One-line verdict

**Consent-gated surveillance-grade collection with named weaknesses** — unchanged in character from the 8.1 assessment, broadened in v9 by new off-device *audio* channels to Meta (live voice + a BLE wearable), with **no covert channel found** by any of the three finders and every collection path permission-gated, node-HITL-gated, and disclosed in tool text; the weaknesses are server-controlled gate flags with unreadable defaults, one hardcoded non-Meta host, under-disclosing OS permission strings, undisclosed Meta-family app-group sharing, and the unverifiable authenticity of the decrypted code.

---

## 2. WHAT CHANGED from 8.1 → 9.1 (the heart)

**Version / provenance.** `CFBundleShortVersionString` 8.1.0→9.1.0; `CFBundleVersion` 1074192126→1080826056; `FBAppVersion` 8.1.0.8.136→9.1.0.17.156; `CFBuildDate` 2026-09-22→2026-09-30 (`prep/ios-infoplist-diff-8.1-9.1.txt`). Integrity shape identical to 8.1: all 5 Mach-Os CMS-verify to Apple Root CA, cryptid 0 (decrypted), the only resource-seal mismatches are the 4 decrypted nested executables, no injected dylib/segment, no trailing bytes (`work/ios-integrity-net/cms_verify.py`, `seal.py`).

**Info.plist / entitlements — almost nothing changed.** Exactly **one** key added: `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` = "This lets you save photos and videos from Muse to your photo library." (`prep/ios-infoplist-diff-8.1-9.1.txt` line 93a94). Entitlements **byte-identical** (`prep/ios-entitlements-diff-8.1-9.1.txt` empty). `UIBackgroundModes` unchanged = `audio/fetch/location/remote-notification` — still **NO `processing`** and **no `bluetooth-central`**. Same `BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers`, same 3 extensions + `MobileConfig.framework`.

**NEW — live voice to Meta (the biggest delta).** An "Alo" speech-to-speech agent, absent in 8.1 (every token 0 in `ipa81` binary): persona string "You are Alo, a personalized AI assistant that is always on built by Meta AI." (`HatchApp` @0x3cb78b0); OpenAI-Realtime-style WebSocket to **`wss://shortwave.facebook.com/vllm_proxy`** (@0x3cb7030) carrying `{"type":"input_audio_buffer.append","audio":"…` (@0x3cb67c0); a separate ASR duplex stream **`wss://shortwave.facebook.com/voyager/v1/asr/duplex`** (`prep/ios91.strings.txt` ~line 144083). ## 3. Surviving findings (locators + tags + proof level)

All findings survived adversarial review — no finding was fully refuted; the `partially_confirmed` votes are folded in as corrections below. Tags reflect the **corrected** criteria. Proof levels: *present* (code exists) / *reachable* (wired to a live path) / *default_on* / *transmitted* — static analysis reached *present*/*reachable* only; **nothing was observed transmitted**.

### New subsystems

**S1 — Alo live voice streams microphone audio to a Meta proxy.** `[GATED]` (UNDISCLOSED contested — see §5). *reachable.* `HatchApp` @0x3cb78b0 ("You are Alo…"), @0x3cb7030 (`wss://shortwave.facebook.com/vllm_proxy`), @0x3cb67c0 (`input_audio_buffer.append`); `ipa81` binary = 0 for every token. ## 4. Strongest evidence FOR and AGAINST the spyware label

**FOR (surveillance-grade breadth into Meta):**
- Off-device data surface now spans camera roll (persistent full-library override, R1), **110** HealthKit types with immediate background delivery (R2), background location SLC (R3), iMessage/Mail forwarded **while locked** (R4), and in 9.1 **live microphone audio** to `shortwave.facebook.com` (S1) plus **ambient wearable audio** to the VM (S2) — all into Meta infrastructure.
- Meta-family shared app groups + keychain enable undisclosed cross-app exchange with other same-team Meta apps (R11); Meta operator SSH into the user's VM (R7).
- Enforcement itself is server-controlled: `node_hitl_enabled`/`server_hitl_enabled` sit in the same MobileConfig as the gate, defaults unreadable (R6); `skip_fbpay_cert_verification` present (R10).
- A hardcoded **non-Meta** host, `www.multimango.com` (S3).

**AGAINST (consent-gated, not covert):**
- **No covert channel found by any of the three finders.** Every collection path is OS-permission-gated + node-HITL-gated + disclosed in tool text.
- The node collection command table is **byte-identical** 8.1→9.1; the only new command token is `voice.audioroute` (R12). New 9.1 commands are all voice/orchestrator/UI, not data pulls.
- Microphone is user-initiated and OS-prompted (and 8.1 already had a mic/speech path); wearable audio sits behind pairing + a consent screen + a per-recording fail-closed owner check (S2); checkout needs an on-device approval sheet (S4).
- Negative sweeps: no covert camera/mic/screen-capture/clipboard **agent** command; no IDFA/ATT; no injected dylibs (R13); no keyboard/VPN/credential/call-directory extension (S9); `BGProcessingTask` inert (R5); BLE background-relaunch inert (S2).

Net: the breadth is surveillance-grade and expanding, but the architecture is consistently gated and disclosed — hence "consent-gated surveillance-grade collection with named weaknesses," not "covert spyware."

## 6. What static analysis cannot settle

- **Authenticity of the decrypted code.** The IPA is a third-party decrypt (cryptid 0, whole-app signature invalid); `__TEXT` instruction/string bytes are readable and internally coherent, but their authenticity cannot be checked against the signature. Every code-behavior claim above is capability/reachability, not proof the shipped Meta build contains these bytes. (HealthKit identifier evidence is the exception — it lives in `__LINKEDIT`, which FairPlay never encrypts.)
- **Live / default values of server flags.** `node_hitl_enabled` (and what it does to enforcement when false), `camera_roll_sync_enabled`, `is_nodes_media_sync_enabled`, `odyssey_server_driven_prepare_purchase`, `voice_entrypoint_enabled`, `skip_fbpay_cert_verification` — none readable statically. So *default_on* vs off, for every gate, is undetermined.
- **Actual transmission.** Per scope, nothing was executed and no host contacted; no byte was observed on the wire. All off-device channels (S1 voice, S2 wearable audio, R1 camera roll, R2 health, S3 multimango) reach *reachable*/*present*, never *transmitted*.
- **Whether operator SSH (R7) and VM silent-push wake are active** for a retail user.
- **The `photo.sync` setter write** (`cameraRollSyncEnabled=true`) was not re-derived at the disassembly level (property-wrapper indirection); carried forward as inference.
- **Gate coverage of the new checkout webview-escalation paths** (S4) — not confirmed to route through the native HITL sheet.

prior_report_corrections: Prior IOS.md section 2 lists an agent command 'geofence.set'. That exact token is NOT present in either the 8.1 or 9.1 binary (only 'geofence.list' and 'geofence.remove' exist as geofence commands; geofence creation is via 'home.bind_geofence'). Minor misnomer, not a behavior change.

Prior iOS reports did not name the LocalMCPServer / MCPBridge / mcp.register_tools layer. It is present in BOTH 8.1 and 9.1 (identical counts) and is the mechanism that exposes the node command table to the agent as MCP tools (with a runtime-immutable tool set). Not a 9.1 delta, but an omission in the prior description of how commands are dispatched.

Prior negative result 'the full node command table has no camera, microphone, screen-capture or clipboard command' remains literally true for the NODE table in 9.1, but is now materially weakened at the app level: 9.1 adds a separate realtime voice path that captures microphone audio and streams it to Meta (wss://shortwave.facebook.com/vllm_proxy) plus a BLE wearable that records audio and uploads it to the VM. Microphone capture is therefore now a live (user-initiated, disclosed) data path even though it is not a node tool.

Counting note: the prior '110 imported HealthKit type identifiers' matches the undef-symbol line count (110) in both builds; nm -u yields 109 distinct HK*TypeIdentifier symbols. The health surface did not grow in 9.1 (0 new identifiers).

votes.corrected_claim: 9.1 adds a new "Alo" speech-to-speech voice agent that is absent from 8.1. It opens an OpenAI-Realtime-style WebSocket session to wss://shortwave.facebook.com/vllm_proxy (a Meta host), captures microphone audio and sends it as base64 audio frames via {"type":"input_audio_buffer.append","audio":"..."}, negotiates a realtime s2s session via {"type":"session.update","session":{"type":"realtime","template":"s2s"}}, and receives streamed audio/transcript back (response.output_audio.delta, transcript deltas). Model IDs are fetched from https://www.multimango.com/api/alo/default-models with a MobileConfig tier fallback. On-device SFSpeechRecognizer is also linked. All Alo/transport tokens count 0 in 8.1 and 1 in 9.1, so the off-device live-audio channel to Meta is genuinely new (delta STRENGTHENED). Proof level is reachable: a full wired state machine exists (Opening Alo session -> connectAndAwaitReady() -> Alo session connected -> recording), but static analysis does not prove default-on or actual transmission. The GATED tag is correct and the gate is strong: session-based voice mode (discrete "Audio recording started/ended: id=" sessions with keep-alive expiry and explicit on-device deletion "finished, deleting from device" -- NOT covert always-listening; "always on" is only the assistant persona for a paired audio wearable), the OS microphone prompt (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, present in BOTH 8.1 and 9.1), NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription, a wearables consent step (HCHPendingWearablesConsent / HatchWearablesOnboarding), a server flag voice_entrypoint_enabled in the server session descriptor, a client aloVoiceEnabled state tied to a paired device, and an in-app "Delete all voice activity?" control over the voice activity log and prompt history. CORRECTION 1: the UNDISCLOSED tag is overstated as a spyware criterion. It is literally true only "relative to the prior reports"; to the end user the voice capture and its transmission to Meta are disclosed (OS mic prompt, "built by Meta AI" persona, and an in-app voice-activity-log/prompt-history with a delete-all control), so it is better labeled new/previously-unreported than undisclosed. CORRECTION 2 (prior report error): the prior iOS report's premise that there was "no microphone capture path" was already wrong for 8.1 -- 8.1 links Speech.framework, declares NSMicrophoneUsageDescription ("talk to Muse ... with your voice") and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription, and uses AVAudioEngine. What is new in 9.1 is specifically the off-device live-audio streaming channel to Meta, not microphone capture per se. One minor imprecision: the field carries base64 audio and the code paths include Opus encode/decode and audio_vq tokens, so "PCM frames" is not certain for every path (PCM16 appears on input; Opus/VQ appear elsewhere).

Microphone audio is captured as Opus by a PAIRED audio-only wearable ("Muse Gadget"), relayed over BLE, decoded to PCM on the phone (AudioConverter/Opus; "Failed to convert Int16 PCM to float buffer"), and streamed out as base64 PCM frames; the phone acts as the network bridge. SFSpeechRecognizer/SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest are newly imported in 9.1, adding on-device transcription. All of this is absent in 8.1 (every Alo/HCHAloRealtimeTransport/"Muse Gadget"/vllm_proxy token = 0 in 8.1), so it is a new off-device live-audio channel to a Meta host. CORRECTIONS to the original finding: (1) "always-on" is model-persona prompt copy ("You are Alo ... that is always on") plus the server-orchestrator description, not evidence the app continuously captures the mic; the real path is gated by voice-mode entry (voice_entrypoint_enabled / aloVoiceEnabled flags) and the mic permission (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription present since 8.1), with a user-facing "voice activity log and prompt history" delete control (assistantVoiceHistoriesDeleteAllConfirmation). TWO parts of the original claim are corrected: (1) "Entirely absent in 8.1" is wrong for the transport layer — the Noise gateway transport (HCHTigonRoutedNoiseGatewayTransport, HCHNoiseGatewayHandshakeOutcome) and the facebook::distribgw / DGWClient layer it rides on are already fully present in 8.1 (exact counts identical: 1/1/17/354), so they are PRE-EXISTING Meta transport infra reused here, not introduced for the wearable. (2) The PERSISTENCE sub-claim (CoreBluetooth state restoration relaunches the app in background) is NOT supported: UIBackgroundModes contains only audio/fetch/location/remote-notification — no bluetooth-central — identical in 8.1 and 9.1, and no CBCentralManagerOptionRestoreIdentifierKey or restore-identifier value string appears in the binary; iOS does not background-relaunch an app for CoreBluetooth state restoration without the bluetooth-central background mode, so the centralManager:willRestoreState: delegate is inert for background relaunch (parallel to the prior "BGProcessingTask likely inert" finding). The GATED description is accurate and corroborated: NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription (present in BOTH versions, unchanged), physical pairing, a logged-in session ("pending recordings for current user but no credentials yet"), a per-recording owner==session-user fail-closed check ("Refusing to upload recording ... owner does not match session user ... fail-closed, leaving pending"), and a "Got file list but sync is not allowed" decision path. UNDISCLOSED holds with nuance: the only Bluetooth consent copy ("Muse uses Bluetooth to search for and provide information on nearby devices and peripherals found") does not disclose uploading recorded audio to a Meta VM. Proof level "reachable" is fair and not overstated — it is neither default_on nor transmitted (cannot be shown statically; requires a physically paired device). Overarching caveat: the binary is a third-party decrypted IPA (cryptid 0); __TEXT code bytes are statically readable but their authenticity is not cryptographically established, so all code-level reachability rests on bytes of unverified provenance.

The core capability is solidly present and new in 9.1, and reachable: the upload log string, the owner-mismatch fail-closed string, the HCHMicroRecordingUploader / HCHDeviceBLEManager / "Muse Gadget" symbols, the OTA firmware strings (Downloading Firmware..., FIRMWARE_UPDATE_SUCCESS, HCHMicroFirmwareManifests), and the encrypted wifi_scan provisioning strings all verify, and a "pending recordings ... retrying uploads" loop plus credential/owner gating indicate live call sites rather than dead type metadata. The prepared ios-strings-new-in-9.1.txt confirms HCHDeviceBLEManager, HCHMicroRecordingUploader, "Muse Gadget", "over the Noise gateway transport" and the owner-mismatch string are new in 9.1; the 8.1 binary yields 0 for the BLE manager/uploader/Muse Gadget. I REFUTE two sub-claims. First, the "Entirely absent in 8.1" framing for the transport: direct strings on the 8.1 binary give identical counts for HCHTigonRoutedNoiseGatewayTransport (1), HCHNoiseGatewayHandshakeOutcome (1), DGWClient (17) and distribgw (354) — the Noise/DGW gateway is pre-existing Meta infra, not part of what 9.1 introduced; evidence block #2 misattributes it to the new feature. The single new distribgw line in 9.1 is only an Obj-C method type-encoding for an RTCDGWConfig signature, not a new transport. Second, PERSISTENCE: the gate text asserts CoreBluetooth state restoration "relaunches the app in background," but the app declares no bluetooth-central UIBackgroundMode (confirmed identical audio/fetch/location/remote-notification arrays in both pristine Info.plists extracted from the source IPAs), and no restore-identifier value or CBCentralManagerOptionRestoreIdentifierKey string exists in the binary. Apple only relaunches an app for CoreBluetooth state restoration when it declares a Core Bluetooth background execution mode; absent bluetooth-central, willRestoreState: can restore in-process state but cannot cause background relaunch, so the persistence vector is inert — directly analogous to the repo's prior BGProcessingTask-inert conclusion. GATED is accurate and well-specified. UNDISCLOSED holds because the capability (off-device upload of wearable audio recordings to a Meta VM) exceeds the generic Bluetooth consent copy, though it sits behind the pairing+session+owner gate. Proof level is correctly "reachable," not overstated to transmitted/default_on. Net: the finding is real and substantially correct about a genuinely new, reachable audio-wearable recording-upload pipeline, but "entirely absent in 8.1" and the PERSISTENCE tag are wrong, so I drop PERSISTENCE and keep UNDISCLOSED + GATED. Operational note for the user: an early plutil call truncated the tree's extracted/v9/ipa/Payload/HatchApp.app/Info.plist to 50 bytes; the guard blocked my restore. votes.reasoning:
I verified all three evidence items and then tested the finding's framing against the 8.1 baseline.

(1) The offsets are exact: 0x34d8200 -> HCHHitlShopifyCheckoutApprovalView, 0x34d8370 -> HCHHitlStripeLinkCheckoutApprovalView, 0x34d7f20 -> HCHHitlCreditCard, 0x34d95a0 -> HCHHitlCheckoutSpendingLimitRow. The full approval-view family is present in 9.1. CONFIRMED present.

(2) odyssey_server_driven_prepare_purchase is at params_map.txt line 6778 in 9.1 and ABSENT from the 8.1 params_map. CONFIRMED new.

(3) payments-graph.facebook.com is in the 9.1 binary (https://payments-graph.facebook.com/graphql) and absent in 8.1, which only had payments-graph.graph.meta.com. CONFIRMED new (as a subdomain expansion).

The refutation: the finding's headline claim and prior_status="new" assert that 9.1 adds the checkout/purchase approval UI. It does not. Diffing HCHHitl classes (strings | grep -oE 'HCHHitl[A-Za-z0-9]+' | sort -u, then comm) shows the entire checkout/Shopify/Stripe/Flight/Browser/CreditCard/SpendingLimit/Terms/Wallet family is identical in 8.1 and 9.1; the only net-new HCHHitl class is HCHHitlApprovalActionGuard. The consumer-facing disclosure ("...make purchases..."), the Stripe Link virtual-card + spending-limit copy, "Approval required," and 3ds_complete_and_authorize are all already in the 8.1 binary. So the capability and its gate pre-date 9.1; they are inherited, not introduced.

What 9.1 actually changes (strengthening): the new-in-9.1 string set contains IAPServerDirected{Payment,PrePayment,Verify}Params, DCPCreatePurchaseQuote/DCPCreatePurchasedOrder mutations, and agentic_escalation_* / checkout_agentic_escalation_iab/_webview/_paypal_webview keys, plus the odyssey flag and payments-graph.facebook.com host. These are server-directed payment plumbing and new webview/PayPal escalation surfaces — a backend/remote-drive expansion of an already-present gated capability. The orchestrator async-dispatch tool description (with "multi-app workflows"/"sending messages") is also new in 9.1 (absent in 8.1).

On the adversarial lens (find the gate / find the gate's weakness): the gate is real and present — a native HCHHitl checkout approval sheet with card, spending limit, terms, and an explicit "Approval required" state, reinforced in 9.1 by the new HCHHitlApprovalActionGuard. But the gate demonstrably covers the native approval views (Shopify/Stripe Link/Flight/generic browser). The new 9.1 escalation paths push checkout into an in-app browser / webview / PayPal webview and include an agentic_escalation_auto_redirect variant; I could not statically confirm these escalation surfaces are gated by the same native sheet. They carry their own _confirmation/_continue_button/_cancel_button keys (suggesting a gate exists there too) alongside _auto_redirect/_redirect_toast (suggesting at least some redirects fire with only a toast). That coverage uncertainty is why I added WEAKNESS: the inherited native gate is sound, but the new escalation-to-webview plumbing introduces a path whose gating I cannot verify statically. Net: verdict partially_confirmed — evidence items true, criteria valid, but the "new in 9.1" / "9.1 adds the approval UI" framing is wrong and the gate-coverage over the new escalation paths is unverified.
